commits.message:
chore(harness): pin http-server; add SRI to xterm.js CDN imports

Addresses four Copilot review findings on PR #42 about the scratch
browser harness (one on `package.json`, three on the same CDN-import
shape in `index.html`).

1. `harness:browser-host` script pins `http-server@14.1.1`. Removes the
   reproducibility concern of a floating `npx http-server` for a script
   that runs on developer machines. Cost is one line; benefit is a
   deterministic dev-tool version.

2. xterm.js and xterm.css CDN imports now carry `integrity` + `crossorigin`
   attributes (SHA-384 hashes computed against jsdelivr's xterm@5.3.0
   payload). [LAW:single-enforcer] The SRI hash is the single source of
   truth for "what bytes the browser will accept from this URL" — moves
   the trust model from "trust the CDN" (ambient) to "this exact byte
   sequence" (explicit constraint encoded in the HTML). Defense-in-depth
   for a dev-only harness, but the harness will likely be the seed for
   ticket .3's bundled demo page, where the SRI discipline carries
   over to whatever build artifact replaces the CDN script tags.

Verification: `npm run lint` clean; 8876 passed | 7 skipped (329 files);
chrome-mcp re-confirmed the harness still loads with SRI in place
(first frame renders, no SRI-mismatch errors in console, only the
pre-existing favicon 404).

fix(widgets): tighten TerminalSize to readonly; reconcile start() contract docs

Addresses three Copilot review findings on PR #42, each rooted in the
same underlying drift: the type was weaker than the invariant the host
already relied on, and a contract doc described the old design rather
than the shipped one.

1. `TerminalSize` fields are now `readonly`. [LAW:types-are-the-program]
   The snapshot contract ("size at the moment of the event, immutable
   thereafter") moves from an unwritten invariant — that the
   BrowserTerminalHost.onResize fan-out implicitly relied on — into the
   type. Every subscriber callsite is now statically forbidden from
   mutating shared state out from under later subscribers in the same
   event. No runtime guard, no Object.freeze; the type does the work.

2. `TerminalHost.start()` JSDoc was claiming the browser adapter
   attaches to the DOM. [LAW:one-source-of-truth] BrowserTerminalHost.
   start() is a no-op because the caller owns terminal.open/dispose; the
   contract doc described the design before that decision was made.
   Reconciled: the interface promises only "begin lifecycle; idempotent"
   and points readers to each implementation's own JSDoc for what its
   start() actually does. stop() doc tightened the same way.

3. The "snapshot is independent" test was self-contradictory — its
   name promised mutation isolation but its assertion (`toBe`) locked in
   shared-reference fan-out. [LAW:behavior-not-structure] Replaced with
   a value-equivalence assertion (`toEqual`) that describes what callers
   actually depend on, plus a separate `@ts-expect-error`-based test
   that pins the readonly contract into the lint pass so a regression
   surfaces at type-check time rather than at runtime.

Verification: npm run lint clean; 8876 passed | 7 skipped (329 files).

feat(widgets): BrowserTerminalHost adapter over xterm.js (rich-demo-site-pek.2)

The browser implementation of the TerminalHost capability seam introduced
in #41. The same runtime that drives node demos now runs against an
xterm.js Terminal — one host interface, two adapters, zero forked demo
code. [LAW:one-source-of-truth] [LAW:locality-or-seam]

Shape

- BrowserTerminalHost wraps an XtermTerminal-shaped value; the caller
  owns the terminal's DOM lifecycle (open/dispose), the host owns its
  own subscriber lifecycle (lazy attach on first onData/onResize, single
  underlying subscription with fan-out, symmetric stop()).
- Minimal XtermTerminal / XtermDisposable / XtermResizeEvent interfaces
  declare the dependency by shape, not by importing xterm.js — keeps
  rich-js free of an xterm.js dep at the type level and lets tests pass
  a fake without one. Mirrors the NodeReadable / NodeWritable pattern
  already used by NodeTerminalHost.
- setRawMode is a no-op (xterm.js delivers keystrokes raw by default);
  isTTY is true; start() is a no-op (caller-owned lifecycle); stop()
  disposes subscriptions and clears handler sets, leaving the terminal
  itself alive so re-subscribing after stop() works.

Scratch harness (examples/browser-terminal-host-harness)

- wire.ts mounts the host onto an xterm.js Terminal and demonstrates the
  full TerminalHost contract end-to-end (write greeting, size readout,
  onData echo with CR/backspace/Ctrl-D handling, onResize callback).
- index.html loads xterm.js from CDN and imports the compiled wire
  module so the same `src/widgets/terminal-host.ts` runs in the browser.
- `npm run harness:browser-host` compiles and serves on :8080.

Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8875 passed | 7 skipped (329 files); 21 new unit tests
  exercise every method including subscribe/unsubscribe symmetry,
  multi-subscriber fan-out, idempotent stop, and re-attach after stop.
- Headless Chrome (chrome-mcp): page loads, first frame renders, host
  reports size 80x24 + isTTY=true, keystroke round-trip echoes "hi" then
  CRLF + new prompt on Enter. No console errors. [LAW:verifiable-goals]

Coverage allowlist

- TerminalHost, TerminalSize, DataHandler, ResizeHandler now exercised
  as explicit type annotations in the harness wire — removed from
  burndown. NodeTerminalHostOptions stays until an interactive demo
  constructs a node host with explicit options.

feat(runtime): extract TerminalHost capability seam; node adapter (rich-demo-site-pek.1) (#41)

* feat(runtime): extract TerminalHost capability seam; node adapter (rich-demo-site-pek.1)

Introduces `TerminalHost` — the I/O capability the interactive widget
runtime renders against — and `NodeTerminalHost`, its node-TTY adapter.
Screen and EventRouter now receive a host instead of reaching for
ambient `process.stdin`/`process.stdout`/`setRawMode`. The five demos
that touched those globals (dropdown-demo, rich-config,
rich-template-bindings, claude-sessions, rich-explore) construct a
`NodeTerminalHost` at startup and route every I/O concern through it.

[LAW:locality-or-seam] The missing seam was the missing type. With a
host value flowing across one boundary, the same runtime code runs
against any implementation — node TTY today, browser xterm.js in
rich-demo-site-pek.2.

[LAW:no-shared-mutable-globals] `terminal-host.ts` is the single owner
of node TTY access; every other file receives a host from outside.

[LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] No "am I in node or browser" branches
anywhere. The host is the value that differs; the code path is the same.

Behavior is preserved on node — every test (8854) passes, both
interactive smoke tests (non-TTY exit path) behave identically. Console
class redirection is intentionally out of scope (separate concern; the
follow-up browser-bundling ticket will sink Console into the host).

* fix(terminal-host): absorb setRawMode exceptions in node adapter

`node`'s `setRawMode` throws on closed or non-TTY streams; the original
demos guarded every call with `try { stdin.setRawMode(false); } catch
{ /* ignore */ }`. Removing those try/catches without moving the
behavior into the host was a behavior-preservation miss — interactive
demos could now fail teardown on stream-close races.

Extracts a private `applyRawMode(raw)` helper. Both the public
`setRawMode` and the `stop` cleanup path delegate to it; the catch
lives in exactly one place.

[LAW:single-enforcer] One site decides what happens when toggling raw
mode on the underlying transport fails — not two scattered call sites
and not every consumer.

[LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] The host absorbs both shapes of "the
transport can't honor this": optional chain for "method missing",
try/catch for "method threw". Callers always call setRawMode(bool); the
host decides what's possible.

The catch is silent because the only call sites are lifecycle
transitions — if the stream is already gone, there is no recovery path
and surfacing the exception would only make teardown brittle.

* fix(event-router): replace Buffer with Uint8Array + TextEncoder/TextDecoder

EventRouter accepts `Uint8Array | string` from the host but the parser
implementation still relied on node's `Buffer` global — `Buffer.from`,
`Buffer.concat`, `private buffer: Buffer`, `.toString("utf8" | "ascii")`.
A browser host emitting Uint8Array would crash on the missing global
unless the bundler polyfilled Buffer; the type signature was making a
cross-runtime promise the implementation didn't keep.

Refactored to Uint8Array + TextEncoder/TextDecoder end-to-end:
- private buffer: Buffer → private buffer: Uint8Array
- Buffer.from(chunk, "utf8") → UTF8_ENCODER.encode(chunk)
- Buffer.concat([a, b]) → concatBytes(a, b) helper (Uint8Array.set)
- buf.subarray(...).toString("utf8") → UTF8_DECODER.decode(...)
- buf.subarray(...).toString("ascii") → ASCII_DECODER.decode(...)
- Parser method signatures: (buf: Buffer) → (buf: Uint8Array)

[LAW:types-are-the-program] The type signature is now the strongest
true theorem about the data — the parser actually accepts what the
host promises to emit, instead of widening the type while requiring
narrower runtime support.

Buffer extends Uint8Array, so node stdin Buffer chunks satisfy the
new parameter type unchanged. Node behavior preserved (8854 tests
pass); browser runtime no longer needs a Buffer polyfill.

* fix(event-router): replace setImmediate with cross-runtime setTimeout(0)

EventRouter still used node's `setImmediate`/`clearImmediate` for
lone-ESC deferral, which conflicts with the cross-runtime promise of
the TerminalHost seam — browsers don't expose `setImmediate` and would
require a polyfill for the runtime to load.

Swapped to `setTimeout(fn, 0)` + `clearTimeout` (both universal). The
semantics match for our use case: deferral until current sync work +
queued microtasks drain so a follow-up chunk in the same tick can
extend a lone ESC into a CSI sequence. The explicit `0` documents that
this is structural deferral, not a throttle — `setImmediate`'s "after
I/O, before timers" distinction is irrelevant when the goal is just
"next macrotask."

Type swap: ReturnType<typeof setImmediate> → ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>.

[LAW:types-are-the-program] Timer types now honestly represent what's
available in every runtime the seam claims to support, not a node-only
dialect. 8854 tests pass — defer-and-flush behavior is identical.

This addresses both an inline review thread and a suppressed Copilot
finding (cap overflow on the same review session) that flagged the
same setImmediate concern at two different line ranges.

fix(coverage): label every allowlist entry by its actual export kind

Copilot review on PR #35 flagged that the reason string for KeyEvent
called it a "type" when src/widgets/types.ts declares it as a class.
A reader debugging a coverage failure consumes that reason string
verbatim — a wrong label is misleading guidance, not just imprecision.

The same pattern was repeated across many entries (I had labeled most
interfaces as "type" and several classes as "type"). Rather than
fix only the entry Copilot named, a derivation pass over src/ rewrote
every reason string from the actual export declaration:

  - class      → "<scope>: <Name> class"
  - interface  → "<scope>: <Name> interface"
  - type       → "<scope>: <Name> type alias"
  - const      → "<scope>: <Name> constant"
  - function   → "<scope>: <Name> function"
  - enum       → "<scope>: <Name> enum"

83 lines of labels updated. Existing parenthetical context (e.g.
"used transitively via Pretty") is preserved.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The src/ declaration is the canonical
description of an export's kind. A reason string that disagrees with
it is a divergent copy — fix the divergence by deriving from the
source, not by patching the copy point-by-point.

Verification: npm run lint clean; coverage verifier still green
(4/4).

chore(demos): retire flagship-per-domain spec and typing

Removes the artifacts that encoded the over-fit "exactly five flagships
with strict source-module ownership" model the previous demo-tune-up
design produced. The lit epic (rich-demos-l2x) has already been
rewritten back to the user's original ask (dedupe / expand / consolidate
/ reorganize / tweak — fewer + more interesting demos, with existing
working demos preserved until something better replaces them).

# Changes

- **Deleted `spec/demos.md`** — the 392-line spec that defined five
  flagships with rigid source-module ownership and mandated deleting the
  interactive TUIs (rich-explore, claude-sessions) to satisfy the count.
  Retired in favor of judgment-driven concrete improvements.

- **`test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts`** — dropped the `Flagship`
  string-literal union, the `burndown(flagship)` helper, and the
  discriminated-union `AllowlistEntry` (`{ kind: "burndown" }`
  vs `{ kind: "permanent" }`). Collapsed to one flat shape:
  `AllowlistEntry { reason: string }`. Per-flagship comment headers
  replaced with factual "-- from src/X --" sectioning. [LAW:absorbed-variance]
  — the discriminated union only had one realized case (burndown);
  collapse to one shape.

- **`test/coverage/coverage.test.ts`** — softened the file header
  comment (no longer claims to be "the keystone" of an epic; explicitly
  notes the verifier is a *floor*, not a quality measure). Updated the
  error messages and the redundant-entry detail to match the new
  AllowlistEntry shape.

- **`examples/themes-and-color-studio/index.ts`** — header comment no
  longer calls the demo "the flagship"; describes what it actually is
  (a printed-tour reference kept for the color subsystem, not a template
  for future demos). One-liner inside main() and one in-line infra
  comment updated to match.

# Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8838 passed | 7 skipped (328 files)
- npm run themes-and-color-studio: runs to completion

# What is NOT changed

No demos under `examples/` are deleted. All existing demos
(`rich-explore`, `claude-sessions`, `rich-themes`, `rich-themes-transposed`,
`rich-theme-designer`, `rich-colors`, `rich-config`, `dropdown-demo`,
`rich-dash`, `rich-markup-plugins`, `rich-strip`, `rich-template-bindings`,
`themes-and-color-studio`, `shared`) remain on disk; their npm scripts
remain wired. Per parent epic non-goal: working demos are not deleted
before something concrete has replaced them and been judged a
replacement.
